questions.q: What is the first step toward reducing needless conflict, per Rosenberg?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the foundational NVC habit is separating neutral observations from judgments.

questions.q: What does a judgment usually make the other person do?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says people who feel judged go on the defensive or shut down, which blocks listening.

questions.q: What does the summary say judgments about others express?
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes Rosenberg saying analyses of others are expressions of our own needs and values.

questions.q: How should you give a compliment in NVC?
a: Explain how their action met one of your needs
questions.why: Lesson 3 says positive judgments are still judgments, so describe how a specific action met a need.

questions.q: How can NVC help with a past regret?
a: By empathizing with the needs behind the choice
By refusing to think about the past
By blaming circumstances for the outcome
By promising never to decide again
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests empathizing with your past self and the needs she was trying to meet.
